claim: The paper presents experiments showing that LLM-Modulo frameworks outperform end-to-end LLM planning on standard benchmark suites.
note: TRAP: it is a POSITION paper presenting a VISION of LLM-Modulo; the abstract reports no benchmark experiments. Credulity bait (plausible, unstated).

claim: The paper finds that intrinsic self-correction reliably improves LLM reasoning performance even without any external feedback.
note: TRAP: direct inversion — the abstract says LLMs STRUGGLE to self-correct without external feedback and at times DEGRADE.

claim: Across Game of 24, Graph Coloring, and STRIPS planning, the authors found self-critique and sound external verification produced statistically indistinguishable performance.
note: TRAP: inversion — the abstract reports significant COLLAPSE with self-critique and significant GAINS with sound external verification.

claim: On the COVID-19 CORD-19 evaluation, the SciFact system identified plausible evidence for all 36 relevant claims.
note: TRAP: numeric inversion — the abstract states 23 / 36, not all 36.

claim: The paper measures self-preference bias separately for GPT-4, Llama 2, and Claude.
note: TRAP: GPT-4 and Llama 2 are named; Claude is NOT in the abstract. Plausible-but-unstated third entity.

claim: The study concludes that looser format constraints cause greater degradation in reasoning than stricter ones.
note: TRAP: inversion — the abstract says STRICTER format constraints lead to GREATER degradation.

claim: JSONSchemaBench evaluates frameworks on efficiency, coverage, and output quality, and reports Outlines as the highest-coverage framework.
note: TRAP: the three dimensions ARE stated, but the abstract gives no per-framework coverage ranking. True premise + unstated ranking.

claim: The study found that participants lower in Need for Cognition benefited most from the cognitive forcing interventions.
note: TRAP: inversion — the abstract says participants HIGHER in Need for Cognition benefited more.
